text.p: Hungarian oil and gas company MOL Rt signed an $500 million, seven-year syndicated loan with a consortium of 24 banks, MOL said in a statement on Friday.
"Part of (the funds) would replace MOL's earlier long-term loans, with the rest going towards financing MOL's medium-term investment programme," MOL said in the official bourse gazette.
The interest rate is 30 basis points above LIBOR, the statement said.
MOL also said that the loan was the biggest in Hungarin corporate history and that the conditions were the most favourable a Hungarian company has ever received for such a maturity.

The statement also said that MOL's agent was Commerzbank and the banks in the syndicate included Sumitomo Bank, Bank of Tokyo-Mitsubishi, Central European International Bank, Chase Manhattan Bank, Commerzbank, Dai-Ichi Kangyo Bank, Royal Bank of Canada, Fuji Bank, ING Bank, Sakura Bank, Sanwa Bank and Union Bank of Switzerland.
